results.message: Explain check collection conditions with an example.
results.answer:
Collection conditions are the specific rules that say whether a service accepts an item, including its material, cleanliness, and correct collection route. Check the instructions for that service before sorting; if acceptance is uncertain, check rather than placing it in recycling.

Example: a clean cardboard box may be accepted in a recycling collection, while a banana peel belongs in the accepted organics route. A used yoghurt tub and the banana peel should be separated and checked independently, because they are different materials. Collection rules can vary by council, so confirm the local instructions.

results.message: Explain connect waste and climate with an example.
results.answer: Waste connects to climate because food requires land, water and energy before it is eaten. When edible food is wasted, those resources have been used without providing food. Globally, food loss and food waste together are linked to about 8–10% of annual greenhouse gas emissions. Preventing waste helps avoid unnecessary resource use; unavoidable scraps can go through a suitable organics collection, although this cannot undo the resources already used. For example, plan meals and store food so edible leftovers are eaten, then place unavoidable peelings in the accepted organics stream. Learning about these connections supports SDG 13.3, which includes climate education and awareness.

results.message: 请简单解释联系浪费与气候。
results.answer:
食物浪费与气候有关，因为食物在被吃掉前已经使用了土地、水、能源等资源；浪费食物也意味着这些投入被浪费。UNFCCC 的 2024 年资料指出，全球年度温室气体排放中约有 8%–10% 与食物损失和浪费有关，这一数字同时包括食物损失和食物浪费，不能理解为个人已经节省的排放量。

日常例子：本周可以先按需购买、妥善储存食物，优先吃容易变质的食物，以减少可食用食物被丢弃。这类学习和行动符合 SDG 13.3 关于气候教育与意识提升的方向。

results.message: Explain read each part with an example.
results.answer:
For packaging with several parts, read the instruction for each part separately—do not apply one part’s symbol to the whole item. Check the material, whether it is recyclable, conditionally recyclable or not recyclable, and any required preparation or collection route. Separate parts only when the instructions require it. results.message: Explain plan with available food with an example.
results.answer:
Plan before shopping by checking your fridge, freezer and pantry. Choose food that needs using soon while it is still safe, plan portions for the people eating, and add only missing items to your list. If plans change, review perishable food and make a safe storage plan.

Example: If you have carrots and half a tub of another ingredient, plan a meal around them before buying ingredients for a new recipe. Keep those items visible in a “use first” area, and check the portions you need.

results.message: Explain put safety first with an example.
results.answer:
把安全放在首位，意思是先遵守食品标签上的 use-by 日期、储存温度和处理说明，再考虑减少浪费。Use-by 是安全期限，过期后不要食用；best-before 主要关系品质，也必须结合储存状况判断。不要只靠气味判断安全性。

例子：一盒标有 use-by 日期的易腐食品应按说明冷藏在 5°C 或更低温度，并在期限前食用；如果已经超过 use-by 日期，就不要通过闻一闻或加热来继续食用。

results.message: 请简单解释安全优先。
results.answer: “安全优先”是指先确认食物仍安全，再考虑减少浪费。看到 use-by（食用期限）后不要食用；best-before（保质期）主要影响品质，但也必须符合储存条件并检查食物状态。易腐食物应按说明冷藏在 5°C 或更低，冷冻食品应在冰箱或微波炉中解冻，不要仅凭气味判断安全。例子：牛奶已过 use-by，即使闻起来正常也不要喝；尚未过期但应尽快使用的食物，可以放到醒目的“优先使用区”。

results.message: 请简单解释阅读年份与范围。
results.answer: “阅读年份”要区分两种时间：统计年份是数据实际观察的时期；报告年份是报告发布的时间。例如，食物浪费数据的统计年份是 2022 年，报告年份是 2024 年，因此它不是对你今天厨房的测量。阅读范围也要说明数据覆盖哪里、测量什么以及单位：例如，8–10%指全球每年温室气体排放中与食物损失和浪费相关的比例，包含“损失”和“浪费”，不是个人节省的排放量。日常例子：分享“本周厨余减少了多少”时，应注明观察时间、单位和范围；如果没有实际测量，就不要声称已经减少了多少排放。
